newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's foreign reserves rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's foreign reserves rise sharply.

text.p: Nigeria's external reserves rose to $4.086 billion currently from $1.413 billion in 1996, military ruler General Sani Abacha announced in his 1997 fiscal budget broadcast on Saturday.

He did not say how the indebted African nation was able to accumulate such external reserves but economic experts believe this is largely due to last year's high prices of crude oil, Nigeria's main export commodity.
The experts say Nigeria seems to be building up its foreign reserves with the ultimate aim of making its naira currency, which now exchanges largely in a free rate, convertible.
Abacha also announced that from January 1, 1997 all contracts entered into in Nigeria would be denominated in the naira currency.
"Hitherto, some contracts entered into in Nigeria had been denominated in both naira and foreign currencies in respect of onshore and offshore expenditure," he said.
"In view of the stability of the naira, with effect from January 1, 1997, all contracts entered into in Nigeria shall be denominated only in naira," he added.
